model.name: Fine-tuned DistilBERT
model.quantization: Dynamic MatMul/Gather, per-channel, reduce_range=True for portable x64 inference

evaluation_protocol.note: Each article is evaluated alone, matching the live prediction endpoint. Dynamic-int8 results can depend on batch composition.

calibration.warning: Calibration on this dataset does not make scores probabilities of factual truth, especially on new topics or sources.

concepts.name: Subword tokenization
concepts.explanation: The pretrained WordPiece tokenizer turns natural text into token IDs. Negations are preserved.

concepts.name: Embeddings and positions
concepts.explanation: Learned token and position vectors represent text and its order.

concepts.name: Multi-head self-attention
concepts.explanation: Queries, keys and values combine contextual information across tokens in six encoder layers.

concepts.name: Feedforward networks
concepts.explanation: Dense layers and GELU activations transform each token representation; a classifier predicts two dataset labels.

concepts.name: Residuals and layer normalization
concepts.explanation: Residual connections and normalization support stable information flow through the Transformer.

concepts.name: Transfer learning
concepts.explanation: All DistilBERT weights are fine-tuned from a pretrained language checkpoint. We did not pretrain or distil the original model.

concepts.name: Cross-entropy and backpropagation
concepts.explanation: Training labels define a cross-entropy loss; gradients update the network to reduce that loss.

concepts.name: AdamW and learning-rate scheduling
concepts.explanation: AdamW, weight decay, warmup, linear learning-rate decay and gradient clipping control training updates.

concepts.name: Dropout and early stopping
concepts.explanation: Dropout regularizes the model. The best validation macro-F1 checkpoint is selected before test evaluation.

concepts.name: Temperature scaling
concepts.explanation: One temperature fitted on validation adjusts model scores. It does not verify real-world facts.

concepts.name: Baseline comparison
concepts.explanation: TF-IDF with logistic regression checks whether the Transformer improves over a simpler text model.

concepts.name: Generalization
concepts.explanation: LIAR short claims are evaluated separately to reveal errors when input differs from training news articles.

sources.name: WELFake
sources.citation: Verma, Agrawal and Prodan (2021), WELFake; DOI:10.5281/zenodo.4561253

sources.name: LIAR
sources.download_note: Original UCSB HTTPS host had an expired certificate during preparation. Used a commit-pinned archive mirror without bypassing TLS verification; test.tsv independently cross-checked byte-for-byte against another mirror.
sources.citation: William Yang Wang (2017), Liar, Liar Pants on Fire; DOI:10.18653/v1/P17-2067
sources.license: Original README permits research use only and says original sources retain copyright. Raw data is not packaged for redistribution.

datasets.split_strategy: WELFake: normalize and group exact title+body text, exact body independent of headline, exact titles of at least six words, identical first 80 words, and approximate near duplicates (64-permutation MinHash, 16 bands; verified 3-word-shingle Jaccard>=0.85 on first512words). Drop contradictory groups and retain one longest representative per group. Stratified seeded 80/10/10 split of unique groups. LIAR original test four-label subset is external-only.
datasets.cleaning: HTML/URLs/whitespace normalization; remove leading publisher datelines, simple bylines, reporting/editing tails and selected publisher title suffixes. Preserve negation, case, numbers and natural wording. Minimum50bodywords for WELFake.
limitations: Approximate grouping cannot guarantee every paraphrase or same-event article is caught.
WELFake combines older datasets; random content-group holdout is not a publisher-held-out or contemporary-news test.
Source writing style and topic can still predict dataset labels after explicit dateline removal.
LIAR short political claims differ substantially from full news articles; external metrics must be shown separately.
External overlap filtering checks exact whole texts only; LIAR claims could still be quoted or paraphrased inside older news articles or have appeared during encoder pretraining.
Dataset labels and model scores are not independent real-time fact verification.

label_audit.publisher_prose_conflict: Zenodo prose incorrectly says 0=fake,1=real. Its checksum-verified CSV has 35,028 label-0 rows and 37,106 label-1 rows, matching the publisher's real/fake totals in the opposite order. Raw Reuters-dateline examples corroborate this mapping.

limitations: Text classification is not live fact verification. No web sources are checked for a prediction.

The TF-IDF baseline sees the full input text while the Transformer uses its first token window; this context-budget difference is disclosed rather than treated as a controlled architecture-only comparison.
Training articles are historical English news, with substantial political and publisher bias. Modern and unfamiliar topics may fail.
Only the first input token window is classified; long articles are visibly marked as truncated.
The independent LIAR test uses short political claims and a documented binary subset; it is not the standard six-class LIAR benchmark.
Removing duplicate articles and some publisher cues does not eliminate all dataset shortcuts or near-duplicates.
The classifier can be confidently wrong. High scores and highlighted text are not evidence that a claim is true or false.
